item.title: Creating, Measuring, and Managing Impact in Complex Service Systems
item.content:encoded:
Ting Yu, University of New South Wales

Ko de Ruyter, King's College London

Che-Hun Liao, Kaohsiung City government

This special issue addresses how research generates tangible impact within complex, interdependent service systems such as healthcare, education, and public administration. Despite growing pressure to prove research impact, evidence of meaningful change in complex service contexts remains limited and difficult to measure due to multiple actors, competing interests, and extended timeframes.

The issue seeks robust empirical evidence showing how research translates into observable improvements in user behavior, service processes, organizational practices, or policy. Contributions using diverse methodologies—qualitative, quantitative, mixed-method, experimental, or participatory—are encouraged. Particularly valued are works addressing how impact is assessed across stakeholders, what roles co-creation plays, and ethical dimensions including power asymmetries, unintended consequences, and underrepresented voices.

Appel publié par European Journal of Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Impact assessment frameworks and metrics in service systems
  • Research impact beyond financial metrics
  • Interdependencies and governance in complex services
  • Impact trajectories and value distribution
  • Change mechanisms and stakeholder engagement
  • Longitudinal and field-based evidence collection
  • Co-creation and stakeholder collaboration
  • Intervention and design-based research outcomes
  • Policy and practice change
  • Scaling and sustainability of research impact
  • Intended and unintended consequences of research
  • Ethical considerations in impact measurement
  • Power dynamics and outcome valuation
  • Differential stakeholder impacts
  • Underrepresented stakeholder voices
  • Managing unequal stakeholder impacts
  • Professional and societal interest alignment
